standard.title: Embedded clauses
standard.description: examine a variety of clause structures including embedded clauses that add information and expand ideas in sentences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can understand complex and compound-complex sentences and how they expand ideas through coordination and subordination (AC9E7LA05). They have not yet examined embedded (relative) clauses specifically — clauses inserted within a main clause to add information to a noun phrase rather than coordinating or subordinating at sentence level.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can examine how embedded clauses function within sentences to add information and expand ideas, and explain their effect.

nodes.label: What embedded clauses are and how they function
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify embedded clauses within sentences and explain how they add information to a noun phrase rather than extending the sentence at its boundary.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two embedded clauses in provided sentences and explain that they modify a noun phrase within the main clause rather than forming a separate clause at sentence level.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and explain how embedded clauses modify noun phrases within main clauses, adding information about people, places or things; distinguish between defining (restrictive) and non-defining (non-restrictive) embedded clauses and explain the punctuation convention difference.
wider: Compare how embedded clauses are used differently in formal academic texts vs informal spoken English, noting how embedding density differs by register
Examine how speechmakers use embedded clauses to add evaluative information in ways that can subtly influence audiences — where the embedded information is presented as given rather than argued
Investigate how embedding multiple clauses creates syntactic density in formal writing, and what this means for readability

response_modes.reason: Students often confuse embedded clauses with subordinate clauses more generally. Encountering them in varied sentence types and text contexts — both formal and informal — helps students distinguish the specific structural feature (noun-phrase modification from within) from related but distinct clause types.

success_criteria: Identifies an embedded clause in a sentence and names the noun phrase it modifies.
Explains why removing the embedded clause would change or reduce the information in the sentence.
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who conflate embedded clauses with subordinate clauses generally will produce structurally incorrect sentences at Node 2 — they are attempting a different grammatical operation. Node 2's writing task requires accurate structural identification of the noun-phrase modification pattern.

nodes.label: Embedded clauses expanding ideas
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how writers use embedded clauses to expand ideas concisely, and use embedded clause structures in their own writing to add information efficiently.
nodes.minimum_width: Write two sentences using embedded clauses to add information about a noun phrase, and explain how embedding is more concise than using a separate sentence for the same information.
nodes.typical_width: Examine how embedded clauses allow writers to pack information into sentences concisely across a range of text types; write extended sentences using embedded clauses and evaluate their effect on the text's tone and density.
wider: Rewrite a passage from an academic text by removing all embedded clauses, substituting separate sentences, and analyse the effect on register and density
Investigate how nominalisation (AC9E8LA06) and embedded clauses work together to create high-density formal prose in informative texts
Create a short formal piece that deliberately exploits embedding to create an authoritative, dense register appropriate for an academic audience

response_modes.reason: Students need to connect their understanding of embedded clause structure to an understanding of writerly choice — when embedding serves the text and when it overloads a sentence. This integration of structure knowledge into purposeful writing is the descriptor's endpoint.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The connection between clause embedding, register, and syntactic density is a rich site for advancing students — moving from identification to genuine stylistic control. Comparative analysis between dense formal prose and lighter informal writing produces meaningful insight into how grammar shapes meaning and effect.
success_criteria: Produces sentences with correctly formed embedded clauses that add information to a noun phrase.
Explains how embedded clauses contribute to concision or information density in a given text.
